name: Kristínartindar
why: The 1126 m top between two glacier tongues, looking across at Hvannadalshnúkur, Iceland's highest peak; back over the heath to Sjónarnípa above Skaftafellsjökull.
book: Free, no permit. Ask at Skaftafellsstofa that morning: the park closes the trail in spring and sometimes into June while the ground thaws. Only in clear weather.
water: No water above Svartifoss; carry 2 litres.
dangers: Steep loose scree to the ridge and an exposed final ridge.
Fog and wind come in fast: the summit is 1100 m above the visitor centre.
Snow patches on the ridge until July.
turnaround: In fog or strong wind turn back at the foot of the scree; be on the summit by 14:00.

points.name: Skaftafellsstofa visitor centre
points.note: Up the Svartifoss path, across the bridge by Magnúsarfoss, then north to Sjónarsker.

points.name: Skaftafellsheiði, at the foot of Kristínartindar
points.note: The open heath of moss and gravel under the peak. From here the steep scree climbs left to the ridge.

points.name: Kristínartindar summit
points.note: 1126 m. Skaftafellsjökull and Morsárjökull on either side, Hvannadalshnúkur (2110 m) across the ice to the east.

points.name: Sjónarnípa
points.note: On the way down by Gláma: the cliff edge straight above the Skaftafellsjökull tongue and its lagoon. Then down by Austurbrekkur to the campsite.
